summary: Authentication for the EINUNDZWANZIG Nostr publishing app. Three login backends share one uniform signer interface (signer.service.js): NIP-07 browser extension (window.nostr, primary path), NIP-46 remote signing via the Amber Android app ("bunker"), and a developer-mode raw nsec held in sessionStorage. session.store.js owns reactive session state (pubkey, profile, authMethod) and persists a reconnect record to localStorage; signer.service.js holds the non-reactive runtime signers (bunker WebSocket pool, in-memory keys). After login the app self-registers the pubkey via POST /api/tracked (which returns first_login and triggers a server crawl) and routes to /onboarding (first login) or /dashboard/articles. Authorization is layered on top via role.store (server-resolved role from /api/me using a NIP-98 signature) and gate.store (feature->required-role registry), enforced by the router beforeEach guard and the useBadgeGate composable.

activities.name: Login with Amber (NIP-46 remote signer)
activities.description: Opens AmberConnectModal. On mount the modal calls prepareAmberConnect() which generates an ephemeral secp256k1 keypair (localSk) + a 16-byte random hex secret, and builds a nostrconnect:// URI of form nostrconnect://<localPubkeyHex>?secret=<hex>&metadata=<json{name,url,description}>&relay=wss://relay.damus.io&relay=wss://relay.nostr.band&relay=wss://nos.lol . The URI is rendered as a 220x220 QR (qrcode lib) and, on Android user agents, as a deep-link button. completeAmberConnect() then awaits BunkerSigner.fromURI on those 3 handshake relays (90s timeout countdown). The user scans the QR in the Amber app and taps Connect; Amber responds on the relays. On success the modal emits {signer,pool,bunkerPubkey,relayUrls,pubkey,localSk}; LoginPrompt calls session.loginWithAmber(payload) which activates the amber signer, sets pubkey, and persists a reconnect record to localStorage key 'nostr-amber-session' = JSON{localSkHex,bunkerPubkey,relayUrls}. On reload restoreAmberSession() rebuilds the BunkerSigner from bunker://<bunkerPubkey>?relay=... without re-scanning. NOTE: a Playwright bot CANNOT scan a QR; to automate Amber it must drive the BunkerSigner handshake out-of-band, OR prefer the nsec path for bot login.

activities.name: Login with raw nsec (developer mode)
activities.description: Opens NsecLoginModal — a two-step modal. STEP 1 (warning): shows XSS-exposure disclaimer with 3 risk bullets; user must click 'I understand — continue' to advance. STEP 2 (form): a password-type input (eye toggle) for the nsec. Submit calls session.loginWithNsec(nsec.trim()) which: validates the string starts with 'nsec1' and nip19-decodes it (buildNsecSigner), builds an in-memory SecretKeySigner via nostr-core, activates the nsec signer, derives pubkey, and stores the raw nsec in sessionStorage key 'nostr-nsec-dev' (NEVER localStorage, NEVER network). On reload restoreSession re-reads sessionStorage; if the tab was closed the key is gone and the user must re-paste. THIS IS THE EASIEST PATH FOR A PLAYWRIGHT BOT TO LOG IN.

notes: CRITICAL FOR A PLAYWRIGHT BOT: There are NO data-testid / aria-label attributes in the auth components — selectors must rely on stable button TEXT (i18n English shown above) and input id #nsec-input. The app uses HASH ROUTING (createWebHashHistory) so the login URL is /#/login (and gated redirects become /#/login?redirect=...). To log in a bot, the nsec path is by far the easiest: navigate to #/login -> click 'More login options' -> click 'Developer mode (nsec)' -> click 'I understand — continue' -> fill #nsec-input -> click 'Continue'. The Amber/NIP-46 path needs a real QR scan by the Amber Android app and is NOT automatable from the browser alone. NIP-07 requires a window.nostr extension to be injected (the 'Connect with Nostr' button is hidden otherwise) — a bot would need to inject a mock window.nostr providing getPublicKey/signEvent/nip44/nip04. Session storage keys: localStorage 'nostr-pubkey','nostr-auth-method'(nip07|amber|nsec),'nostr-amber-session'(JSON), and sessionStorage 'nostr-nsec-dev'(raw nsec, tab-scoped). The signer is wired through services/signer.service.js module-level singletons (NOT on window) via activateSigner; everything signs through signEvent()/signerCapabilities(). After login, POST /api/tracked('self') returns first_login deciding /onboarding vs /dashboard/articles; ?return=<relative path> on the login route overrides the destination (validated to be same-origin relative). Authorization gates: role.store fetches /api/me with a NIP-98 signature (each forced refresh triggers a wallet/signer prompt; 30-min TTL cache in localStorage 'badge-role-cache-v1'); gate.store caches the feature->role registry ('badge-gates-cache-v1', 5-min TTL). Router guard enforces meta.requiresAuth, meta.requiresBadge (feature-keyed, e.g. magazines), and meta.requiresRole ('admin' for /dashboard/gates and /dashboard/system). Gates fail OPEN during cold start / network errors to avoid flashing denied. Role hierarchy free<member<manager<admin. Dependencies on other domains: profile (VerifiedAccountsModal republishes kind:0, opened from ProfileEditModal), draft (scheduleConvergingRefresh after login), settings (hydrateFromBackend), onboarding (crawler status API).

summary: The longform article editor for the EINUNDZWANZIG Nostr publishing platform. Users write NIP-23 longform articles (kind 30023) in a Milkdown markdown editor with separate metadata sidebar (title, summary, cover image, hashtags, optional author pubkey). Content can be saved as a local-only draft (autosave to localStorage), a shared draft on relays (kind 30024), or an encrypted self-to-self draft (kind 31234 / NIP-37), or published as a final article (kind 30023). Three content formats are supported behind one editor surface: standard markdown Article, Gallery (frontmatter type: gallery), and Interview (frontmatter type: interview). A separate Articles list view drives an inspector drawer for site assignment, engagement, comments and NIP-09 deletion. All write paths are backend-first then relay-publish, and every authoring action requires an authenticated session with an active Nostr signer.

notes:
AUTH GATE: All /dashboard/* routes require auth (meta.requiresAuth). Saving to relays, encrypted drafts, publishing, and deletions all require an active Nostr signer (signEvent). Encrypted draft save THROWS if signer supports neither NIP-44 nor NIP-04 — extension/nsec signers work, some won't. DRY-RUN STOP POINT: 'Save locally' (type=local) and autosave write ONLY to localStorage and sign/publish NOTHING — use this to test the editor without emitting Nostr events. Autosave fires on DEBOUNCE_AUTOSAVE interval and on unmount-if-dirty, so navigating away can silently persist a local draft.

KEY GOTCHAS for a Playwright driver: (1) The editor is at /dashboard/editor (NOT in CreatorPage.vue — CreatorPage is the public /u/:npub profile and contains NO editor). (2) dTag/identifier and slug are NOT user-editable in the UI — dTag is auto-generated 'draft-<Date.now()>' for new articles or inherited from the resumed draft/article key. (3) There is NO scheduling UI: published_at is always set to now at publish time. (4) There is NO explicit language, canonical/source URL, visibility/gating, or site/magazine assignment field inside the editor itself. Site assignment happens AFTER publish via the ArticleInspector drawer in the Articles view (siteStore.assign/unassign, see sites domain). Magazine assignment is read-only in the inspector and managed in the magazine issue editor (separate domain). Canonical-URL / source is only set programmatically by the RSS importer via extraTags ['source', feedUrl] (imports domain), not via the editor form. (5) Cover image upload forces a 1.91:1 crop (1200x630); inline images are uncropped. Uploads go through Blossom (useBlossom → mediaStore.upload), depends on media/settings domain for configured servers. (6) Save-draft is a split button: main button opens a 3-item dropdown (local/shared/encrypted) — items use @mousedown.prevent, so Playwright should mousedown rather than rely on click+blur (the menu closes on blur after 150ms). notes:
AUTH: every /dashboard/* route requires auth (meta.requiresAuth on the parent). Sites routes have NO requiresBadge/requiresRole gate (unlike magazines which need requiresBadge:'magazines'). So any logged-in user can create/manage sites. All writes are signed Nostr events via auth.service.signEvent, so a signer (NIP-07/local key) must be available.

PUBLISH MODEL: site.store uses a 5000ms debounce (PUBLISH_DEBOUNCE_MS) for assign/unassign/reorder, batching rapid changes into one 30004 publish per site; pendingPublishCount/pendingPublishDeadline are exposed for UI countdown; flushPendingPublishes() drains on unload/logout. There is also a draft-mode (isDraftMode/toggleDraftMode/publishDraftAssignments/discardDraftAssignments) that batches assignments without publishing until committed. Wiki section config saves use a SEPARATE 900ms debounce in SiteOrganizer (updateSiteConfig). publishSite/publishSiteConfig are backend-first (apiService.submitEvent) then relay publish; they only throw if BOTH backend and all relays fail.

DTAG: derived once at create from the title slug and is immutable thereafter (config.slug is a display/routing field but the curation set d-tag stays the original). dTag is the route param :siteId everywhere and the public URL /s/:dTag.

DATA SOURCE: fetchSites pulls from apiService.listSites (REST) and then per-site apiService.getSite for article a-refs; configs arrive inline (s.config) — fetchSiteConfigs is now a no-op. Article titles/images/tags for Organize/SiteDetail come from useArticleStore (must be fetched; Organize views trigger articleStore.fetchArticles).

DEPENDENCIES: article domain (SiteAssignPopup lives there for membership), media domain (MediaPicker), relay.store (write relays), session.store (pubkey), toast.store, activityLogger. SiteAssignPopup.vue and SiteGroupManager.vue appear to have no live importers within the sites views scanned (assign UI is invoked from articles components; group manager looks legacy/board).

notes:
AUTH/GATES: All four magazine routes require auth (requiresAuth on /dashboard) AND meta.requiresBadge:'magazines'. The router guard (router/index.js beforeEach) calls gateStore.fetchGates(); if the 'magazines' gate is enabled and required_role != 'free', it refreshes roleStore and redirects to AccessDenied (query gate=magazines, role=<required>, from=<path>) when the user's role rank is below required. So a Playwright run must use an account whose role meets the magazines gate, or the gate must be free/disabled.

NOSTR KINDS: magazines and issues are BOTH kind 30004 (KIND_CURATION_SET). Magazine event carries tag #t magazine + d=mag:<slug>, plus one 'a' tag per issue ref. Issue event d=<mag:slug>:issue-N, content is JSON {sections, coverArticle, coverImage, coverSubtitle}, with 'a' tags for article refs and a published_at tag. Magazine CONFIG is kind 30078 (KIND_APP_DATA), d=einundzwanzig:magazine-config:<slug>. Constants: MAGAZINE_PREFIX='mag:', MAGAZINE_CONFIG_PREFIX='einundzwanzig:magazine-config:'.

PERSISTENCE MODEL: Issue drafts are stored in a BACKEND DB (apiService.saveIssueDraft / listIssueDrafts / deleteIssueDraft), not as Nostr events; only on Publish does an issue become a signed relay event. There's a one-time migration of old localStorage 'magazine-issue-drafts' into the backend (loadIssueDrafts) which toasts toast.draftMigrated. Publish/config/magazine writes are 'backend-first': submit to apiService.submitEvent, then relay-publish; relay-only fallback if backend fails; only throws if neither backend nor any relay accepted.

DEPENDENCIES: IssueEditor relies on articleStore (article library + getArticle by aRef for titles/images), mediaStore via MediaPicker, and the magazine config (accent color, issue number) for the live preview. Public pages /m/:slug, /m/:slug/:issueId are NOT in this SPA router — they are Flask server-rendered (see router comment), so Playwright verifying the public output must hit the backend, not the hash-routed SPA.

CREATE-MAGAZINE FAILURE UX: on createMagazine error the store toasts toast.magazineCreateError with an action 'openSettings' linking to /dashboard/settings (relay setup), since publishing needs write relays.

feed.store.js (in scope per task) is RSS-subscription state (kind 30078 d=einundzwanzig:feed-sources, debounced 5s publish). It is unrelated to magazine UI components and exposes addFeed/removeFeed/markFetched/updateFeedTitle/loadFeeds/flushPendingPublishes used by the Subscriptions feature, not the magazine views.

GOTCHA: section.articles items can be legacy strings or {aRef,featured} objects; code defensively handles both (_migrateSection). coverArticle <select> only offers articles already assigned to a section.

summary: The social/engagement domain covers all reader-facing interactions with content in the EINUNDZWANZIG platform: liking (reactions), reposting, bookmarking, commenting, and Lightning zapping of articles and short notes; a profile-anchored "Pinnwand" wall (NIP-22 kind 1111 posts/replies with client-side muting); the two-panel drag-and-drop board for organizing articles into sites; and a localStorage-backed activity timeline. Engagement actions publish Nostr events (kinds 7, 16, 6, 1111, 10003, 9734) signed by the active signer, are mirrored to the backend via apiService.submitEvent, and use optimistic counts that converge on backend-crawled tallies. Article engagement is aRef-scoped (useEngagement + comment.store/bookmark.store), while note/wall engagement is event-id-scoped (useNoteEngagement + event-engagement.store). The board and activity log are local organizational tools that do not publish engagement events.

notes:
AUTH GATES: All engagement publish actions (react/repost/bookmark/comment/zap on articles AND notes/wall) require both session.pubkey set AND isSignerActive() true — useEngagement._requireSession / useNoteEngagement._requireSession toast 'engagement.errNotLoggedIn' and abort otherwise. Wall top-level/reply posting also needs session.pubkey (composer opens unauth on creator page but shows a sign-in hint and cannot send). Dashboard routes (/dashboard/*) are meta.requiresAuth=true; the public creator page /u/:identifier is unauthenticated.

WALL COMPOSE GATE: top-level wall compose is ONLY rendered when WallPanel prop allowTopLevelCompose=true, which is set only on CreatorPage (/u/:identifier). The dashboard own-wall (subscriptions 'wall' tab) is read+reply only.

ZAP GATES: target author profile must have lud16 or lud06 (else 'engagement.errNoLightning'); LNURL endpoint must be NIP-57 capable (allowsNostr + nostrPubkey); amount bounded by endpoint min/maxSendable (msat). Payment precedence is NWC wallet (wallet.store, globally-mounted WalletPaymentConfirm) > WebLN (window.webln) > QR fallback. The QR path cannot confirm payment, so counts only converge via the staggered refresh once the kind 9735 receipt propagates.

OPTIMISTIC COUNTS: Article counts read from article.engagement.* + per-instance pending delta; refresh schedules REACTION_SCHEDULE_MS=[3000,8000], ZAP_SCHEDULE_MS=[3000,8000,20000]; deltas only retire once the server count catches up by the delta. Note/wall counts read from event-engagement.store (backend /engagement/by-event/batch + /refresh, 200ms debounce, 50-id batches, 60s TTL); if the backend route 404s, counts show zero + local optimistic deltas (one console.warn).

CROSS-DOMAIN DEPENDENCIES: EngagementBar/NoteEngagementBar are mounted by the ARTICLES domain (ArticleInspector, ArticleGridCard, ArticleListItem), the SUBSCRIPTIONS domain (NoteCard with target kind=KIND_NOTE/1), and the wall. Board drag/remove actions ultimately republish site list events via site.store (SITES domain) after a ~5s debounce — not published here. Activity log entries are WRITTEN by other domains via activityStore.log(); this domain only displays/filters/clears them. Comment publish lives in useEngagement.js, not comment.store (store only owns the list + optimistic overlay). Mute list is localStorage-only, keyed by visitor pubkey.

KIND CONSTANTS (constants/nostr.js): KIND_REACTION=7, KIND_GENERIC_REPOST=16, KIND_NOTE=1, KIND_COMMENT=1111, KIND_ZAP_REQUEST=9734, KIND_ZAP_RECEIPT=9735, KIND_PROFILE=0; bookmark list kind 10003 (hardcoded in bookmark.store); note repost uses kind 6 for kind-1 targets (NIP-18, in eventBuilder.noteRepost). Comment maxlength=2000, zap comment maxlength=280, zap presets [21,100,500,1000] default 100. NoteEngagementBar intentionally has NO bookmark button (article-aRef scoped only).

summary: User-facing profile and account settings for the EINUNDZWANZIG Nostr publishing dashboard. Covers editing the user's own Nostr profile metadata (kind 0, NIP-24 fields), managing external identity claims (NIP-39 `i` tags), viewing NIP-58 badges, configuring relays (custom relay roles plus the user's NIP-65 kind-10002 relay list), and configuring Blossom media servers (publishable as kind 10063). Also includes a global read-only profile peek modal (subscribe/unsubscribe) triggered by avatar clicks anywhere in the app. Profile/identity/relay-list/blossom-list writes are signed via the active Nostr signer (NIP-07 / NIP-46 / nsec) and published to relays, with optimistic backend import.

notes:
AUTH: All /dashboard/* routes require auth (router meta requiresAuth:true on the /dashboard parent). Publishing profile/identity/relay-list/blossom-list events requires an active signer (NIP-07 extension, NIP-46/Amber, or in-memory nsec) via auth.service.signEvent; nip98.service.signRequest throws Nip98SignError('NO_SIGNER') if isSignerActive() is false (used for backend admin writes, not directly in these profile/settings publish paths).

KINDS PUBLISHED: profile metadata = kind 0; NIP-39 identity changes republish kind 0 with `i` tags; NIP-65 relay list = kind 10002; Blossom server list = kind 10063; Blossom uploads sign kind 24242 auth events (not published to relays). Badges are read-only here (NIP-58 kinds 30008/30009/0); badge creation is delegated to external BadgeBox (rinbal.badgebox links throughout).

LOCAL vs NOSTR: Adding/removing/editing custom relays and Blossom servers is purely localStorage (keys: custom-relays, custom-relay-roles, hidden-bootstrap-relays, blossom-servers, tag-subs, author-watchlist, locale, articles-view-mode). These do NOT publish to Nostr until 'Edit relay list' (kind 10002) or 'Publish to Nostr' (kind 10063) is used. settings.store has cross-tab sync (storage event) for author-watchlist and tag-subs only.

GOTCHAS: ProfileEditModal merges edits onto the latest raw kind:0 (fetchLatestProfileEvent) so unknown fields/tags survive; empty form fields DELETE the corresponding kind:0 key. Identity wizard uses profileMetadataRaw to avoid clobbering content. relayService.publish gives each relay an 8s timeout (default) and returns {successes,failures}; success requires >=1 relay OR backend import OK. Blossom: primary server = upload target, others = mirror targets; default servers cannot be removed (only custom). 100 MiB hard ceiling (BLOSSOM_MAX_FILE_SIZE). ProfileModal subscribe/unsubscribe depends on subscription.store domain (kind 30000 follow set). Relay sections start collapsed and cap at 10 rows per section.

summary: This domain covers four dashboard workspaces of the EINUNDZWANZIG Nostr publishing hub: (1) Imports — subscribe to external RSS/Atom/JSON feeds, preview items, review images, and import articles as private encrypted drafts (kind 31234 wrapping kind 30024); (2) Subscriptions — a NIP-51 follow set (kind 30000, d=subscriptions) plus a reading Feed panel and a Pinnwand/Wall tab (kind 1111 comments); (3) Media — a Blossom-backed media library (BUD-02/04, kind 24242 auth) for upload/list/delete/copy/crop; (4) Matrix — a spreadsheet that assigns articles to sites by toggling membership of curation sets (kind 30004 via site.store). All routes live under /dashboard which requires auth; none has an extra badge/role gate. Many actions are debounced relay publishes (5s) with optimistic local state.

notes: AUTH/GATES: All four routes are children of /dashboard which sets meta.requiresAuth=true (router beforeEach redirects to /login?redirect=...). No additional requiresBadge/requiresRole on matrix/media/subscriptions/imports (unlike magazines which needs badge 'magazines', or gates/system needing role 'admin'). NOSTR KINDS observed: imports save kind 31234 (NIP-37 encrypted draft) wrapping kind 30024 (longform draft) — NOT published to relays publicly until user publishes; requires signer NIP-44 or NIP-04 (imports fail-fast otherwise). Subscriptions = kind 30000 (NIP-51 follow set, d='subscriptions'), separate from kind 3 contacts. Wall/Pinnwand tab = kind 1111 (NIP-22 comments) handled by wall.store (outside strict file scope). Feed-source list persisted as kind 30078 d='einundzwanzig:feed-sources' via feed.store (feed.store.js is outside the named scope but is the backing store for ImportsView). Matrix assignment publishes kind 30004 (KIND_CURATION_SET) by republishing the whole site event via siteService.publishSite (site.store.js). Media uploads/deletes/list use Blossom BUD-02/04 with signed kind 24242 auth events (blossom.service.js). DEBOUNCE: subscription.store and site.store both use 5s debounced publish with optimistic local state and Undo windows (manage modal unsubscribe undo absorbs the publish entirely). DEPENDENCIES: ImportsView depends on feed.store, draft.store, relay.store, settings.store (Blossom servers), session.store (pubkey/signer). FeedPanel/wall depend on subscription-feed.store and wall.store. MediaPicker/ImageCropDialog are reused by editor/site/profile forms (not standalone routes). RSS scope limits: newest10/25/50 + sinceVisit(=RSS_MAX_LIMIT 500); RSS_DEFAULT_LIMIT=25; batches >5 items paced 250ms. Image rehost default ON; deselected images stay as original source URLs. STORES NAMED IN SCOPE NOT BACKING THESE VIEWS: creator-media.store.js, creator-content.store.js, matrix-ui.store.js, rss-discovery/naddr/parser services are helpers; matrix-ui.store.js was not wired into MatrixView (which uses useMatrixPage composable + site.store/article.store instead).

summary: NWC (Nostr Wallet Connect, NIP-47) wallet integration plus Lightning zap orchestration. A single per-browser-profile wallet is connected via a NWC URI (persisted in localStorage, survives reloads and Standup login/logout). Once connected, a sticky status bar exposes a wallet hub for viewing balance/transactions, sending payments (BOLT-11 invoice, Lightning Address, LNURL-pay), receiving (creating a BOLT-11 invoice with QR, or redeeming a LUD-03 LNURL-withdraw). Zaps (NIP-57 kind 9734 zap requests) for articles, notes, wall posts, and creator profiles are prepared by zap.service and paid via a precedence chain: connected NWC wallet (globally-mounted WalletPaymentConfirm modal) > WebLN browser extension > QR/copy fallback. The wallet itself never signs the zap request; a Nostr session signer does.

notes:
AUTH/PERMISSION GATES: (1) The wallet itself needs NO Standup login — it is per-browser-profile, persisted in localStorage ('nwc-connection'), works for logged-out visitors and survives login/logout. Wallet ops (connect, send, receive, pay) only require an active NWC connection (wallet.isConnected). (2) ZAPS require BOTH: a connected/usable Lightning path AND a logged-in Nostr session with an active signer — because the kind 9734 zap request is SIGNED by the visitor's Nostr identity, not the wallet. CreatorPage.openZap redirects to /login when !session.pubkey even if a wallet is connected; useEngagement._requireSession enforces session+isSignerActive() with toast engagement.errNotLoggedIn.

NOSTR KINDS: only kind 9734 (KIND_ZAP_REQUEST) is published in this domain — three variants in event-builder.service.js: zapRequest (article, a-tag), noteZapRequest (event id, e+p tags), profileZapRequest (p-tag only). Kind 9735 (zap receipt) is referenced in builder docs but is published by the LNURL provider, not this app. NWC traffic (kinds 13194/23194/23195/23196 etc.) is internal to nostr-core's NWC client, not surfaced here.

MOUNTING: All six wallet components are mounted ONCE in PublicShell.vue. WalletPaymentConfirm has no props — it is purely driven by wallet.store.queuedInvoice, so any caller anywhere opens it via wallet.requestPayment({invoice,hint}) and awaits the promise (resolves {preimage} on pay-success, rejects with code USER_CANCELLED / BUSY / NOT_CONNECTED). Modal stacking is controlled by PublicShell refs (openSend/openReceive close the detail hub first).

GOTCHAS: connectionUri is intentionally NOT exposed on the store (spending secret). Store-level locks: isPaying (payInvoice), isMakingInvoice (makeInvoice) guard against double-spend/double-create. Generation-token guards drop late async replies after disconnect/swap. Receive settlement detection is push-based via payment_received → lastSettledPaymentHash (no polling). Send modal accepts amountless invoices visually but the pay path needs a decodable invoice; LNURL amount is bounds-checked twice (client computed + lnurl.service). Transactions page size = 6, hasMore is a heuristic (full page == maybe more). Payment precedence everywhere: NWC > WebLN (window.webln) > QR/copy fallback.

DEPENDENCIES on other domains: apiService.getProfile (resolve author lud16/lud06), session.store (signer/pubkey for zaps), relay.store + event-builder + auth.service.signEvent (sign 9734), toast.store (all feedback), i18n keys under wallet.* / engagement.* / creatorPage.*. External libs: nostr-core (NWC, lnurl, bolt11), qrcode.

summary: This domain is the application backbone of the EINUNDZWANZIG Nostr long-form publishing platform: the Vue Router route table with auth/role/badge guards, the two layout shells (AppShell dashboard chrome and PublicShell for public creator pages), the global Cmd+K command palette, the Flask backend API client (used instead of live relay queries for reads), the unified multi-backend signer (NIP-07 extension / NIP-46 Amber bunker / in-memory nsec), and the central event-builder catalog that constructs every unsigned Nostr event the app publishes. The router uses hash history; all `/dashboard/*` routes require auth, magazines require a feature-gate badge, and `gates`/`system` require the admin role. The event-builder service is the single source of truth for every Nostr KIND the platform emits.

notes:
AUTH/GUARDS: router uses createWebHashHistory so all URLs are hash-prefixed (e.g. https://host/#/dashboard/articles) — Playwright must navigate to the # form. router.beforeEach: any route with meta.requiresAuth triggers sessionStore.restoreSession() (async, awaits Amber reconnect); unauthenticated -> redirect /login?redirect=<fullPath>. Feature gate (meta.requiresBadge='magazines') fetches gates+role and redirects to AccessDenied with query {gate,role,from} if role rank < required (only enforced when gate.enabled && required_role!='free'). Role gate (meta.requiresRole='admin' on gates+system) always enforced via role rank. Role hierarchy default ['free','member','manager','admin'].

VISIBILITY (not security): sidebar v-show and command-palette filtering hide magazines (hasAccess('magazines')), gates+system (role==='admin'). These are UI-only; the router guards are the real gate.

READS vs WRITES: All reads go through the Flask backend (apiService, SQLite populated by crawler) NOT live relays — fast path. Writes are built by eventBuilder -> signed by signer.service -> published to relays (RELAY_GROUPS) AND/OR submitted to /api/events. Per-user endpoints (tracked, tags, rss/fetch, me, managed feed, all admin gate writes) use NIP-98 signed Authorization (kind 27235) via nip98.service — every such call may trigger a signer/wallet prompt.

DEPENDENCIES: This domain depends on session.store, gate.store, role.store, relay.store/relay.service, wallet.store (NWC), comment.store, zap.service, auth.service. The actual form fields for article/draft/profile/site/magazine editing live in views/dashboard/* (out of this file scope) — event KIND catalog and tag structure documented here is authoritative for what gets published. Public site/magazine routes (/s/:slug, /m/:slug) are NOT in this Vue router — they are server-rendered by the Flask backend.

RELAY_GROUPS: profiles, longform, discovery, general, fallback (constants/nostr.js). Visitor actions publish to RELAY_GROUPS.general and use general[0] as relay hint. Amber NIP-46 handshake relays are a fixed separate set (damus, nostr.band, nos.lol).
